name: Launch trajectory tracking and projected insertion
description: Reconstructs a launch ascent from altitude and speed telemetry (ground track, downrange, flight-path angle, instantaneous impact point, each sample's osculating apsides, and the insertion orbit at engine cutoff), and projects the insertion orbit of a scheduled launch from its pad, liftoff time, target orbit and a comparable flight's profile, including the liftoff times that join a reference plane.

sequentialJustification.detail: Deterministic geometry over caller-supplied telemetry, target orbits and reference ephemerides. No host calls, threads, orbit propagation or network access.

inputPorts.description: $LAM with LAUNCH_EPOCH, LAUNCH_DATA.SITE, TARGET_ORBIT inclination and pass direction, SPEED_REFERENCE, and TIME_FROM_LAUNCH_S / ALTITUDE_M / SPEED_M_PER_S samples so far; an ASCENT_EVENTS cutoff is optional.

outputPorts.description: $LAM (TELEMETRY): reconstructed samples, Earth-fixed TRAJECTORY_OEM, instantaneous impact points and apsides, and INSERTION with BURN_OUT_VECTORS once cutoff is reached.

wildcardJustification.detail: Phase, azimuth, cutoff, insertion elements and the latest sample as JSON; the result is the $LAM frame.

outputPorts.description: Phase, azimuth, cutoff, insertion elements and the latest sample as JSON; the result is the $LAM frame.

inputPorts.description: $LAM with LAUNCH_DATA.SITE, LAUNCH_EPOCH or a launch window, TARGET_ORBIT (inclination or PLANE_REFERENCE, pass direction, insertion time, optional apsides), SPEED_REFERENCE, and a comparable flight's TIME_FROM_LAUNCH_S / ALTITUDE_M / SPEED_M_PER_S profile.

outputPorts.description: $LAM (PROJECTED): nominal samples, Earth-fixed TRAJECTORY_OEM for launch screening, INSERTION with BURN_OUT_VECTORS, and IN_PLANE_LIFTOFF_EPOCHS for a reference plane.

wildcardJustification.detail: Azimuth, insertion elements and in-plane liftoff times as JSON; the result is the $LAM frame.

outputPorts.description: Azimuth, insertion elements and in-plane liftoff times as JSON; the result is the $LAM frame.
